et diplom.explanation: "Et diplom" means "a diploma". To talk about a small certificate for taking part in something, use "et diplom for deltagelse" (a certificate for taking part): "Alle børn fik et diplom for deltagelse" (All the children got a certificate for taking part).

et distrikt.explanation: "Et distrikt" means "a district". To talk about the area a school covers, use "et skoledistrikt" (a school district): "Vi bor i samme skoledistrikt" (We live in the same school district).

et dobbeltværelse.explanation: "Et dobbeltværelse" means "a double room". It is built from "dobbelt" (double) and "et værelse" (a room). To book one, say how long you stay with "til" (for): "Jeg vil gerne booke et dobbeltværelse til to nætter" (I would like to book a double room for two nights).

et dokument.explanation: "Et dokument" means "a document". To tell someone to save one on the computer, use "at gemme" (to save): "Husk at gemme dokumentet" (Remember to save the document).

et download.explanation: "Et download" means "a download". It comes from the English word. The action is "at downloade" (to download): "Jeg downloader filen" (I am downloading the file).

et drab.explanation: "Et drab" means "a killing". To say what a news story is about, use "om" (about) after the verb: "Avisen skriver om et drab i Aarhus" (The paper writes about a killing in Aarhus).

et drama.explanation: "Et drama" means "a drama". To say someone makes a big fuss over little, use it for the fuss: "Hvorfor al det drama?" (Why all the drama?).

et drivhus.explanation: "Et drivhus" means "a greenhouse". To say what you grow there, use "at dyrke" (to grow): "Vi dyrker agurker i drivhus" (We grow cucumbers in a greenhouse). The part "drivhus" is also in "drivhuseffekten" (the greenhouse effect) and "drivhusgasser" (greenhouse gases).

et drømmejob.explanation: "Et drømmejob" means "a dream job". It is built from "en drøm" (a dream) and "et job" (a job). Here "drøm" means a wish, not a dream you have while you sleep: "Hendes drøm er at blive kok" (Her dream is to become a cook).

et dukketeater.explanation: "Et dukketeater" means "a puppet theater". It is built from "en dukke" (a puppet or doll) and "et teater" (a theater). The part "teater" is also in "et børneteater" (a children's theater).

et dusin.explanation: "Et dusin" means "a dozen". To say a dozen of something, put the thing right after it, with no word for "of": "et dusin roser" (a dozen roses).

et dynebetræk.explanation: "Et dynebetræk" means "a duvet cover". It is built from "en dyne" (a duvet) and "et betræk" (a cover). The part "betræk" is also used for furniture: "et sofabetræk" (a sofa cover).

et dyr.explanation: "Et dyr" means "an animal". To talk about an animal that lives free in nature, say "et vildt dyr" (a wild animal): "Vi så et vildt dyr i skoven" (We saw a wild animal in the forest).

et dyreinternat.explanation: "Et dyreinternat" means "an animal shelter". To say you take in a pet from there, use "at adoptere" (to adopt): "Vi adopterer en hund fra et dyreinternat" (We are adopting a dog from an animal shelter).

et dæk.explanation: "Et dæk" means "a tire / deck". When you talk about the rubber part of a wheel, use it for the tire: "Jeg skal have nye dæk til bilen" (I need new tires for the car). When you talk about a floor of a ship, use it for the deck: "Skibet har tre dæk" (The ship has three decks).

et døgn.explanation: "Et døgn" means "a day (24 hours)". To say something is open all day and night, use "hele døgnet" (all day and night): "Butikken er åben hele døgnet" (The store is open all day and night). Do not mix it up with "en dag" (a day), which can also mean only the daytime: "Det er lyst om dagen" (It is light during the day).

et dørslag.explanation: "Et dørslag" means "a colander". To say you rinse vegetables in it, use "at skylle" (to rinse): "Jeg skyller grøntsagerne i dørslaget" (I rinse the vegetables in the colander).

at efterkomme.explanation: "At efterkomme" means "to comply with". To say someone did what a request asked, put the request after it: "Han efterkom anmodningen" (He complied with the request).

at efterlade.explanation: "At efterlade" means "to leave behind". To say you left a message, use it with the message: "Jeg efterlod en besked" (I left a message). Do not mix it up with "at forlade" (to leave a place): "Hun forlod byen" (She left the city).

at efterligne.explanation: "At efterligne" means "to imitate". The noun is "en efterligning" (an imitation). To say a thing is a fake copy, use it: "Tasken er en efterligning af en dyr taske" (The bag is an imitation of an expensive bag).

at efterlyse.explanation: "At efterlyse" means "to call for / search for". To say the police ask the public for help, put what they look for after it: "Politiet efterlyser vidner" (The police are appealing for witnesses).

at efterspørge.explanation: "At efterspørge" means "to demand / ask for": "Folk efterspørger flere cykelstier" (People are asking for more bike lanes). The noun is "efterspørgsel" (demand): "Der er stor efterspørgsel på billige boliger" (There is high demand for cheap homes). Do not mix it up with "at kræve" (to insist on getting): "Jeg kræver mine penge tilbage" (I demand my money back).

at eje.explanation: "At eje" means "to own". To say you simply have something with you, use "at have" (to have) instead: "Jeg har penge på mig" (I have money on me).

at eksistere.explanation: "At eksistere" means "to exist". To ask whether something is there, Danish uses "at findes" (to exist, to be there): "Findes der en bus?" (Is there a bus?)

at eksperimentere.explanation: "At eksperimentere" means "to experiment". To name what you try out, add "med" (with): "Vi eksperimenterer med nye opskrifter" (We are experimenting with new recipes).
